mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous year same month by > 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer confidence and spending, which negatively impacts corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate and a decline of more than 1% in payroll employment (PAYEMS) month-over-month signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > previous month +0.4pp AND PAYEMS monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered events.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, in the absence of a concurrent GDP contraction, signals aggressive tightening that immediately raises risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.75pp AND GDPC1 not contracting YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such events.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of more than 0.3% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a decline in consumer spending (proxied by GDPC1) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a softening economic outlook and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.3% AND GDPC1 monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals entrenched manufacturing weakness, which reliably precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such four-month sequences.
